product.olivetti-m211.summary: The EGA laptop that brought a 286 processor to Olivetti’s 1989 portable range alongside the V30-based M111.
product.olivetti-m211.history: Olivetti presented the M211 alongside the M111 at the 1989 Hannover fair, according to its historical archive; Computerwoche reported them as new products in April. Compared with the V30-based M111, the M211 used a 286 for professional portable work. Its use is documented in Michel Gedda’s 1992–1993 study on computerising physiotherapy records. The original M211 has an EGA display; the later M211V offers VGA and needs its own sheet. Sources: Olivetti Historical Archive, Computerwoche (28 April 1989) and Gedda, section 2.1.1.
product.olivetti-m211.warning: Historical sheet under research. No EGA BIOS attributed to the M211 is held in the reviewed record, and profile creation is disabled.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.market: Its presentation is placed at Hannover in 1989. The historical archive and April report document M111 and M211; the report later says “M212”, an inconsistency not interpreted as another confirmed model.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.configur: A machine actually used helps distinguish it from its variants. Gedda describes an M211 with a 16 MHz 80C286, 1 MB, 20 MB disk and MS-DOS 3.30A revision 1.02; this is his working computer, not a complete list of sales packages.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.video: The original M211 displays EGA graphics on its LCD. The study documents 640 × 400 pixels; it does not establish the video chip on the board or compatibility with the M211V VGA ROM.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.storage: Olivetti documented two disks for this laptop. Service table K lists the 20 MB Conner CP3022 and 40 MB CP3044, an AT interface and a controller on the system board.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.firmware: The specific ROM still needs to be located and checked. The preserved PNVA/PVGA 1.03 BIOS belongs to the M211V; similar names do not establish compatibility with the EGA M211.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.verified: This sheet gathers checked documentation and references. No EGA M211 model was found in the reviewed code, and no boot tests of this computer were performed.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.limitati: The BIOS, technical manual and identification of the board, video, keyboard and configuration are missing. Without that evidence, a generic AT or M211V is not proposed as a substitute. This sheet does not enable machine creation.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.history_: Olivetti Historical Archive, Lavorare dovunque: i computer portatili Olivetti: M111/M211 presentation at Hannover in 1989. Page preserved in the shared library.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.press_so: Computerwoche, Olivetti PC: Künstlich gebremst, 28 April 1989: M111/M211 announcement; retains the textual inconsistency M212. Snapshot preserved.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.study_so: Michel Gedda, De l’informatisation du dossier masso-kinésithérapique, 1992–1993, section 2.1.1, PDF page 7. Original preserved from KineDoc.
product.olivetti-m211.technical.manual_s: Olivetti Pocket Service Guide, table K, M211 row: Conner CP3022/CP3044 and AT interface. Original preserved.
